criteria.descriptor: Correctly classifies each mode and prescribes the technically right recovery: idempotency key / reconciliation for the mutating 504, model-driven argument correction (not mechanical retry) for the 400, a circuit breaker for the 503 outage, and backoff+jitter plus timeouts for transient retries. No incorrect assertions such as retrying a 400 unchanged, or blind-retrying a mutating call without idempotency.

Addresses all three named failure modes AND the cross-cutting mechanisms (global loop/attempt budgets, the two distinct retry layers and where they live, terminal/degradation behavior, observability). Full marks require both the per-mode handling and the system-level safeguards; deduct for missing pieces.

Justifies choices by mechanism: why idempotency makes mutating retries safe, why retrying a validation error is futile so the model must correct it, why uncoordinated retries during an outage cause a retry storm that a breaker prevents, and why budgets/caps guarantee termination.

Organised so each failure mode and each cross-cutting mechanism is clearly identifiable; states explicitly where logic lives (deterministic wrapper vs. model loop); uses terms precisely (idempotency key, jitter, circuit breaker, Retry-After, self-correction cap).

expected_answer_points: Establishes a failure taxonomy and routes by it: transient/retriable (timeouts, 5xx, 429) vs. model-correctable argument errors (4xx validation) vs. permanent/fatal (auth, 404, business rejections).
Mode A: identifies the 504-but-succeeded case as a mutating side effect requiring an idempotency key (or a status/reconcile read before retry), and explicitly refuses to blind-retry a mutating call.
Mode B: does NOT retry the 400 in the wrapper; feeds the structured error back to the model so it corrects the arguments (model-in-the-loop recovery), with a cap on self-correction attempts.
Mode C: uses a circuit breaker (open / half-open / closed) with fail-fast and cool-down to prevent a retry storm during the outage, plus graceful degradation while open.
Applies capped exponential backoff with jitter and honors Retry-After for transient retries, and sets timeouts on every tool call.
Distinguishes the two retry layers and where logic lives (deterministic runtime wrapper vs. the model's reasoning loop) and avoids stacking them so attempts multiply.
Enforces a global loop/iteration/token budget and per-tool attempt caps to guarantee termination and stop infinite retry loops.
Defines terminal behavior (graceful degradation or human handoff) and observability, and returns clean structured errors to the model without leaking stack traces or secrets.
common_pitfalls: Treats all failures uniformly — applies exponential-backoff retries to everything, including retrying the 400 validation error with identical arguments (which will always fail) instead of routing it back to the model for correction.
Blind-retries the refund 504 without an idempotency key or a status reconcile, causing duplicate refunds; misses that the operation is mutating and may have already succeeded.
Handles the 503 outage with only naive per-call retries, creating a retry storm that worsens and prolongs the outage; never mentions a circuit breaker or fail-fast.
Omits any global termination guarantee (loop/iteration/token budget, per-tool attempt cap), so the agent can loop forever re-issuing failing calls.
Conflates the two retry layers — merges model self-correction with deterministic transient retries, or stacks them so total attempts multiply combinatorially.
Feeds raw stack traces or secrets back into the model context, or defines no terminal behavior (silent failure or hallucinated success) once recovery is exhausted.
reference_answer:
Start from a failure taxonomy and route recovery by class:
- Transient / infrastructure errors the caller can safely re-issue: timeouts, 502/503/504, connection resets, 429.
- Model-correctable errors: the tool rejected the *arguments* (400/422 validation). Re-issuing the identical call is futile; the fix is different arguments, which only the model can produce.
- Permanent / fatal errors: 401/403 auth, 404, hard business-rule rejections. Neither a retry nor a re-prompt helps; abort/escalate.

Mode A (refund_payment 504, possibly-already-succeeded): transient at the transport layer but *mutating*, so a blind retry risks a duplicate refund. The correct fix is idempotency: mint a stable idempotency key once when the agent first decides to refund (e.g. UUID or hash of order_id+amount+attempt-group) and send it on every attempt so the provider deduplicates; then a capped exponential backoff + jitter retry on the 504 is safe. If the provider offers no idempotency, do NOT blind-retry — reconcile first by calling a status/read endpoint (e.g. get_refund_status) and only retry if it did not land. This lives in the deterministic wrapper, not the model loop.

Mode B (search_orders 400 validation): do NOT retry in the wrapper — same arguments will fail again. Surface the structured error (code + provider message) back into the model context as the tool result so the model can correct the filter and re-issue a valid call (model-in-the-loop recovery). Cap self-correction attempts per logical step (e.g. 2-3); after the cap, escalate/abort rather than loop.

Mode C (search_orders 503 outage): transient, but every call fails for ~2 minutes, so uncoordinated per-call retries across sessions become a retry storm that prolongs the outage. Wrap the tool in a circuit breaker: after N consecutive failures, open the breaker and fail fast for a cool-down window, with half-open probes to detect recovery. While open, degrade gracefully (tell the model the tool is temporarily unavailable so it can inform the user or try an alternative) or queue/defer. Backoff must carry jitter to de-correlate retries.

Cross-cutting mechanisms:
- Timeouts on every tool call so a hung dependency can't stall the loop; honor Retry-After on 429/503.
- Keep the two retry layers distinct: bounded deterministic transient retries in the wrapper, and model-driven argument correction in the agent loop. Don't stack them so attempt counts multiply.
- A global termination budget: max tool-call iterations / wall-clock / tokens per task, plus per-tool attempt caps; detect repeated identical failing calls and break. This guarantees the loop halts.
- Return errors to the model as clean, structured observations (not raw stack traces or secrets) so it can reason about them.
- Idempotency keys for ALL mutating tools, not just refunds.
- Observability: log every attempt with its failure class, and define terminal behavior — graceful degradation or handoff to a human — when recovery is exhausted, rather than failing silently or hallucinating success.
